name: git show
shortDescription: Show various types of Git objects. Most commonly used to view the details and diff of a specific commit.
detailedDescription:
The `git show` command displays detailed information about Git objects — usually commits. By default, it shows the last commit (HEAD): the author, date, message, and the full diff of changes introduced.

Unlike `git log`, which shows a list of commits, `git show` dives deep into a single commit. It's the command you use when you want to answer: 'What exactly did this commit change?'

It can also display tags (showing the tag message and the tagged commit), tree objects (directory listings at a specific commit), and blob objects (file contents at a specific commit).

parameters.description: The commit to show. Can be a hash, branch name, tag, or relative reference like HEAD~3.
Show the contents of a specific file at a specific commit. For example, `git show HEAD~2:config.js`.
Show only file change statistics instead of the full diff.
Show only the names of changed files.
Control the output format of the commit header. Accepts `oneline`, `short`, `medium`, `full`, or custom format strings.

examples.title: Show the latest commit in detail
examples.description: See what was changed in the most recent commit.
examples.code:
git show

# Shows: author, date, message, and full diff

examples.title: Show a specific commit
examples.description: Inspect any commit by its hash.
examples.code:
git show a1b2c3d

# Or relative references:
git show HEAD~3    # 3 commits ago
git show main~5    # 5 commits before main's tip

examples.title: View a file at a specific commit
examples.description: See exactly what a file looked like at any point in history.
examples.code:
# View package.json as it was 10 commits ago:
git show HEAD~10:package.json

# View a file from a specific branch:
git show feature-api:src/server.js

examples.title: Quick summary of a commit's changes
examples.description: See which files were affected without the full diff.
examples.code:
git show --stat a1b2c3d

# Output:
# src/app.js    | 12 ++++++------
# src/utils.js  |  4 ++++
# 2 files changed, 10 insertions(+), 6 deletions(-)

commonMistakes.text: `git show` shows ONE object. For viewing multiple commits, use `git log`. For comparing two commits, use `git diff commit1..commit2`.
Use `git show <commit>:<path>` to view old file versions without checking them out. Great for quickly referencing old code.
